notes:
Account summary
- Mid-market SaaS building an LLM-powered support agent for end-user ticket deflection + agent assist.
- Primary pain: inference cost volatility and limited explainability. Quote (PM): “Our CFO is asking why inference cost went up 18% last month when usage only went up ~5%.”
- Strong interest in Redwood Optimize levers (batching/caching/quantization profiles) but wants measurement/diagnostics first.

Workload / traffic profile
- Workloads: chat (streaming) + summarization (non-streaming), some embeddings for doc retrieval.
- Concurrency: spiky during business hours (US), plus nightly backfill summarization runs.
- Typical output lengths vary widely; they suspect long-tail outputs drive cost and latency outliers.

Key requirements (from calls + emails)
- Unit economics: wants a clear definition of blended $/1M output tokens that can be reconciled against platform usage + infra spend assumptions.
  - Asked explicitly for drilldowns by model and region; also wants to separate interactive (streaming) vs batch jobs.
  - Wants contributing signals to explain changes: cache hit rate, batching utilization/efficiency, avg output length, quantization profile.
- Performance: keep P95 under current baseline (they wouldn’t commit to a cost win that worsens UX).
- Controls: wants to understand what Redwood auto-tunes (continuous batching, cache) vs what they can configure per route.
- Deployment: starts on hosted API for speed, but may need Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput during peak support hours.
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logging. No strict EU residency requirement (US-only is fine). Interested in VPC if Dedicated.

POC discussion (current shape)
- Goal: demonstrate 10–20% improvement in $/1M output tokens on 2 representative routes without degrading P95 latency.
- Compare: baseline configuration vs (a) caching-enabled route + (b) batching policy changes.
- Measurement request: daily summary and a simple breakdown (route/model/region) + flags for streaming vs non-streaming.

Competitive context
- Currently evaluating multiple paths: “stay on Bedrock”, “move to an LLM API provider”, or “invest in self-hosted + a runtime.” They’re looking for a pragmatic path that doesn’t add ops headcount.
- They like the idea of Dedicated as a middle ground but want proof that cost reporting and optimization are real (not hand-wavy).

Internal Redwood notes
- This account is a good fit for the Unit Economics dashboard initiative: they are explicitly asking for cost transparency and diagnostics (cache/batching signals).
- Important to be careful with messaging: internal unit economics dashboard is not customer-facing. Offer an export or a one-off analysis for POC, and set expectations.
- Suggested stakeholders to pull in for the metric-definition conversation: Rishi Malhotra (FP&A methodology owner) + Nadia Rahman (token metering).
